baseline.reason: Exact bug and unaffected output lines matched the shared three-version Docker replay.; meta.json's root cause is exactly reproduced end-to-end. dwa_uncompress() computes `dc_w = td->xsize >> 3` / `dc_h = td->ysize >> 3` (floor) in the intro commit (cc85ca1c), and `dc_w = (td->xsize+7)>>3` / `dc_h = (td->ysize+7)>>3` (ceil) in the fix commit (c911e0001115). The per-block DC index `idx = (x>>3) + (y>>3)*dc_w + dc_w*dc_h*j` is used only to READ `dc[idx]`; for a non-8-aligned dimension the outer x/y loop still visits `ceil(size/8)` blocks, so with the buggy floor-based dc_w/dc_h the last block's read aliases onto a different (smaller) index than the one a correctly-sized/encoded buffer intends for it -- i.e. it reads outside the intended per-block sub-region of the shared dc_data array. I verified mathematically (idx_buggy(x,y,j) <= idx_fixed(x,y,j) pointwise for every position, since dc_w_buggy<=dc_w_fixed and dc_h_buggy<=dc_h_fixed always) and confirmed empirically that this specific mismatch is always contained within the DWA thread buffer's generous allocation (av_fast_padded_malloc adds ~2x + rounding + 64-byte headroom), so for any dc_count consistent with the image geometry this manifests as a silent wrong-slot READ rather than an ASan-detectable heap overflow; a deliberately tiny/inconsistent dc_count (e.g. dc_count=0) does crash under ASan, but it crashes BOTH post_intro and post_benign identically (confirmed empirically), so it is not diagnostic of this specific fix and was not used as evidence. Instead I built a precise behavioral oracle isolating the exact aliased slot. Results, identical command/input across all three builds: pre_intro fails to decode at all (\"Compression 8 is not implemented ... patches welcome\") because DWA decoding did not exist before the intro commit, so the flaw cannot manifest there (intro_verified=yes: the bug is reachable only starting at the intro commit, which is the commit that introduces DWA decoding with the floor-division bug baked in from the start). post_intro decodes and prints PIXEL_G=PIXEL_B=PIXEL_R=0.9999998807907104, exactly matching to_linear(half(8.0)/8)=to_linear(1.0)=1.0 -- i.e. it read the WRONG DC slot (20) that the floor formula aliases the last block onto. post_benign decodes (with the fix's own added avpriv_request_sample \"odd dimensions DWA\" notice) and prints PIXEL_G=PIXEL_B=PIXEL_R=4876797.5, matching to_linear(half(64.0)/8)=to_linear(8.0)=exp(2.2)^7≈4,876,797 -- i.e. it read the CORRECT DC slot (23) that the ceiling formula assigns to that block. The observed post_intro value is wrong by six orders of magnitude and traces precisely to the labeled off-by-rounding root cause; pre_intro and post_benign both complete without exhibiting it (pre_intro because the feature is absent; post_benign because it reads the correct slot).
